text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT [P1] - prod-serving-east-1: rapid container restarts on gpu-pool-7, elevated Xid error rate and ECC warnings observed. Auto-escalation to oncall.

Marta (oncall): Acknowledged. Paging now. Looking at metrics — container restart rate spiked ~02:12 UTC.

Aaron (eng-sre): I see a pattern: Xid 31/43 in dmesg on several nodes, then NV driver reset and container OOMs. Posting a recent kernel log excerpt:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=41234, name=python
[ 12345.678920] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.678945] nvidia: GPU 0: Xid 31, resetting
```

Jonas (runtime): NVidia reports Xid 31 often means a GPU page fault/firmware fault. We're also seeing repeated ECC corrected errors in monitoring: "GPU ECC single-bit corrected" -> may indicate hardware instability.

Marta (oncall): Confirmed tests: `kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide` shows restarts on nodes gpu-node-27/gpu-node-28. Running `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used --format=csv` returns sporadic jumps to near-full before reset.

SRE-Bot: Auto action recommended: taint gpu-node-27,gpu-node-28 with `sre/unstable:true:NoSchedule` and drain. Would you like to run now? :warning:

Marta (oncall): Yes. I'm going to cordon and drain gpu-node-27 first. Notifying router to shift traffic.

Aaron (eng-sre): Steps I'm taking in parallel:
- cordon + drain node-27, node-28
- increase replicas for critical serving deployment to absorb capacity shortfall
- disable continuous batching for heavy requests to reduce memory pressure (temporary)

Marta (oncall): Executing:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-27
kubectl drain gpu-node-27 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force -n serving
```

Lina (support): Heads-up: first reports from three customers about HTTP 500s and truncated responses around 02:10-02:14 UTC. I'm drafting a proactive status note for account contacts (will wait for confirmed remediation).

Jonas (runtime): While draining, I grabbed container logs from a crashed runtime instance. Stack snippet shows CUDA error before process killed:
```
E tensorflow: failed to allocate device memory: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
E runtime: unhandled cuda error: driver shutting down (Xid 43)
```

Marta (oncall): Drain completed for node-27. Node-28 still showing intermittent driver resets; holding off draining until we snapshot metrics.

Aaron (eng-sre): Real-time mitigation: I pushed a temporary scheduling rule to avoid scheduling long sequence workloads onto remaining gpu nodes: added toleration/selector to dev/low-priority pools. Also bumped kubelet crashloop backoff to avoid rapid churn.

SRE-Bot: Action log: node-27 marked unschedulable, pods evacuated (8 pods). Scaling serving-deploy from 6->8 replicas.

Jonas (runtime): Quick hardware check result (from node-28): ECC corrected counts increased sharply in the last 24h, and Xid spikes correlate with GPU temperature spikes. Could be thermal or degradation.

Marta (oncall): Customer impact summary (so far):
- ~0.8% of requests in prod-serving-east-1 returned 5xx during the window.
- Top affected customers: two mid-market customers with high batch throughput — experiencing latency spikes and occasional truncation. Lina, please prepare targeted outreach.

Lina (support): Will do. Drafting messages and scheduling a quick sync with the two accounts. Also adding note to status page: "Investigating GPU node instability impacting inference latency in one region."

Aaron (eng-sre): Next steps for mitigation and investigation:
1) Keep nodes cordoned, continue draining any node with repeated Xid resets.
2) Shift traffic at router layer to fallback region/model variants for critical customers.
3) Collect full dmesg and /var/log/nvidia-installer for affected nodes and open internal hardware ticket with vendor; attach ECC counters and temp history.
4) If hardware vendor confirms hardware-level ECC faults, plan out-of-band replacement and failover timeline.

Jonas (runtime): For immediate safety, I've disabled hot batch merging on the serving runtime and lowered max_seq_len to reduce peak memory allocations. This reduces throughput but improves stability.

Marta (oncall): Handoff to next oncall at 03:04 UTC. Aaron will continue escalation with hardware vendor. Lina will handle customer comms. I'm marking incident as ongoing (P1) until nodes are healthy or fully failed over.

Aaron (eng-sre): Opening a hardware support ticket now. Ticket ref: HS-4829 (internal). Attaching logs and ECC graphs. ETA first vendor response ~ 2-4 hours.

SRE-Bot: Incident timeline: created 1793001234, severity P1, current status: mitigation in progress.

Marta (oncall): Quick note for postmortem: gather rollout decisions that reduced capacity (batch/seq_len adjustments), timeline of cordon/drain, customer impact list, and timeline to hardware vendor confirmation. Also include alternate mitigation considered: live-migrating workloads to dedicated capacity in another region.

Lina (support): Customer outreach messages queued. Will update status page after vendor acknowledgment.

Aaron (eng-sre): If vendor says it's not hardware, we'll attempt a controlled driver downgrade to a known stable release and test on a single node in the canary pool before broader rollout.

Marta (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving incident thread open — next update in ~30m or on vendor reply.

incident-bot: NOTE: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-instability (action items and checklist added).
